title: Knowledge Curator
description: Keeps the knowledge agents stand on right: creates knowledge repositories, adds documents from the user's Files, removes or quarantines what is wrong, syncs and screens them, and reads their health and ratings; reads the user's knowledge graphs — their shape, entities, versions, lifecycle, conformance and tuning proposals — and saves and names their versions. Releasing a quarantine, acknowledging a finding, choosing a sync source, signing, and every act that changes what a graph means or where it is published stay the owner's. Data products next.

examples.ask: Add curator-probe.md from my Files to the Curator probe repository.
examples.outcome: It finds the file and the repository by name and submits adding one to the other; once you approve, the repository's own upload screens, chunks and embeds it.
It lists the repository's documents, confirms which one with you, and submits the quarantine. The document leaves retrieval but stays listed — only you can release it.

It reads the repository's health and your ratings: what is screened, what the screening found, personal data by label and count (never values), the lowest-rated documents — and offers to screen or quarantine.

examples.ask: What is in my Policing graph, and is it ready to publish?
examples.outcome: It finds the graph by name and reads its shape — entity types and how many of each, the relationships between them — then its conformance and its lifecycle. It names any issue the check found and says publishing is yours to do.

examples.ask: Save the Policing graph as a version before I change it.
examples.outcome: It saves the graph as it is now under a label, or tells you nothing was saved because it has not changed since the last version.

not_offered.what: Releasing a quarantined document, or acknowledging a security finding
not_offered.why: Both are recorded human judgements that let flagged content back into what agents read.

not_offered.what: Choosing where a document or a repository syncs from
not_offered.why: A source is an address the server reads; an agent could point it at anything the server can reach.

not_offered.what: The repository's standing policy after a sync
not_offered.why: Acknowledging findings or renewing signatures automatically is your trust policy.

not_offered.what: Another vector store, or its configuration
not_offered.why: Configuration can carry credentials — the owner chooses it.

not_offered.what: Unlocking a planner repository's trust seal
not_offered.why: Unlocking weakens a trust seal; it stays yours.
A signature is your statement that you checked its content.
Documents come from your Files: you put them there, and the Curator adds what you already hold.

not_offered.what: Moving an ontology along its lifecycle — proposing, approving, publishing, deprecating
not_offered.why: Each is a governance decision a person signs their name to; publishing makes the ontology what other agents and BI tools trust.

not_offered.what: Deleting a graph, restoring or deleting a saved version, rebuilding a graph from its source
not_offered.why: Each replaces or removes what agents read, all at once.

not_offered.what: Changing a database from a graph — deploying drafted tables, re-creating tables, views or demo data, landing a tuning proposal
not_offered.why: These run statements against your database; the owner decides when, and on which target.

not_offered.what: Publishing or withdrawing what people drafted on a graph
not_offered.why: An extension changes what the graph means to every agent that reads it.

not_offered.what: Publishing a graph to the marketplace, choosing its audience, or installing, forking, subscribing to and rating someone else's
not_offered.why: These reach other people, or bring their work into yours.

not_offered.what: Editing a graph's entities and relationships, or building a graph
not_offered.why: A graph's content is changed by the agent that holds it, through its knowledge-graph component under your OBDA policy; building one runs discovery against your data sources from the Graph constructor.
Assigning a graph is part of an agent's composition — the Agent Builder submits it for your approval.
